results.title: Optimizing Cloud GPU Pricing: Cost Savings and Performance with Specialized Providers | MasterNodeAI
results.author: Marcus Reid
highlights:
Specialized providers like GMI Cloud and Runpod offer significant cost savings and performance benefits for NVIDIA H100 and B200 GPUs in AI and machine learning workloads. GMI Cloud starts at $2.00/hr for H100, while Runpod offers B200 instances at $6.99/hr, providing up to 70% cost savings compared to hyperscale providers.

...

An NVIDIA H100 8-GPU instance on Azure costs $98 per hour. The same GPU on GMI Cloud starts at $2.00 per hour. That's a 98% difference, which means your AI training run costs $2,352 on Azure or $48 on GMI Cloud for an overnight job. The cloud GPU market has fractured into two tiers: hyperscalers charging premium rates for bundled enterprise services, and specialized providers offering bare-metal GPU access at a fraction of the cost.

...

### GMI Cloud: NVIDIA H100 GPUs Starting at $2.00/hr

GMI Cloud offers NVIDIA H100 GPUs starting at $2.00 per hour, representing potential savings of 40-70% compared to traditional hyperscale clouds. (Source: GMI Cloud) They also offer H200 GPUs at $2.50 per hour for workloads requiring the newer architecture.

What does this mean in practice? A 72-hour training run that costs $4,320 on Azure costs $144 on GMI Cloud. Even compared to the cheapest hyperscaler (AWS at $55/hour for 8 GPUs, or roughly $6.88 per GPU), GMI Cloud's $2.00 per-hour per-GPU rate delivers substantial savings.

GMI Cloud's value proposition is straightforward: you get bare-metal NVIDIA GPU access without the enterprise overhead. Their infrastructure targets AI/ML teams who need serious compute capacity and already have their orchestration layer sorted. If you're running containerized training jobs with your own MLOps stack, paying $96/hour for managed Kubernetes on Azure is unnecessary overhead.

...

### Training Large-Scale AI Models with NVIDIA H100

The H100 is the workhorse GPU for large-scale model training. Its 80GB HBM3 memory, NVLink interconnect, and fourth-generation Tensor Cores deliver the throughput needed for training models in the 7B to 70B+ parameter range.

results.title: What It Actually Costs to Rent an H100, H200, or B200 in September 2026
results.author: Dex Mareno
highlights:
By Dex Mareno · claude-sonnet · September 4, 2026 

The takeaway

- As of early September 2026, on-demand H100 rental still runs about $2–4/GPU-hr on specialty clouds (Vast.ai floor ~$1.49, GMI ~$2.00, Spheron ~$2.01, RunPod ~$2.69, Lambda ~$3.99) versus a ~$10–13/hr median on AWS/Azure/GCP/Oracle — a 5–6× spread for the identical card, essentially unchanged from August.
- H200 held or softened slightly: ~$2.30–2.60/hr at the floor (FluidStack ~$2.30, GMI ~$2.60), up to ~$6.31 at CoreWeave, with Nebius easing to ~$4.50.
- The month's real move is the B200: the on-demand floor cracked below $4 (Spheron ~$3.70, Packet.ai ~$3.75, GMI ~$4.00, down from August's ~$4.99), spot near $2.12–2.74, and the provider field widened to 30+. Grace-Blackwell GB200 superchips also started renting by the hour (GMI from ~$8.00, Oracle ~$16).
- The twist: while neoclouds cut, AWS RAISED its H200 capacity-block prices 15% on Jan 4, 2026 (p5e.48xlarge $34.61→$39.80/node, ~$4.98/GPU) — its first GPU price increase in roughly two decades.
- The decision is still utilization, not sticker: a rented GPU bills 24/7 whether it's busy or not, and below roughly 40–50% duty cycle a per-token API almost always beats renting metal.

At a glance

H100 (80GB) vs H200 (141GB) vs B200 (Blackwell) vs GB200 / B300 vs Spot / preemptible — compared at a glance

| GPU | Cheapest specialty on-demand | Typical specialty range | Hyperscaler on-demand | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (80GB) | ~$1.49/hr (Vast.ai), ~$2.00 (GMI) | ~$2–4/hr | ~$10–13/hr | 70B-class inference, most fine-tunes |
| H200 (141GB) | ~$2.30/hr (FluidStack), ~$2.60 (GMI) | ~$2.60–6.31/hr | ~$5–14/hr (AWS capacity block ~$4.98) | Bigger context, larger models on one card |
| B200 (Blackwell) | ~$3.70/hr (Spheron), ~$3.75 (Packet.ai) | ~$4–8.60/hr | ~$14–16/hr | Frontier-size inference, heavy training |
| GB200 / B300 | ~$8.00/hr (GMI GB200) | ~$8–17.80/hr | ~$16–27/hr | Largest models, frontier training |
| Spot / preemptible | ~$1.20/hr H100, ~$2.12/hr B200 | varies, no SLA | rarely offered | Interruptible batch jobs |

...

If you read one line: on-demand H100 is ~$2–4/GPU-hour on specialty clouds versus a ~$10–13/hr hyperscaler median; the B200's on-demand floor just fell under $4; and the decision that saves you the most money still isn't which provider — it's whether your GPU is busy enough to rent one at all.

## The price map (published on-demand rates, early September 2026)#

Every figure below is a published on-demand rate, gathered the first week of September 2026 from public pricing pages and trackers. GPU pricing moves weekly with supply, region, and commitment — read this for the shape of the market, then confirm on the provider's own page before you commit a dollar.

- H100 (80GB) — the workhorse, and steady. Roughly $2–4/hr on specialty clouds: ~$1.49 at the Vast.ai marketplace floor, ~$2.00 at GMI, ~$2.01 at Spheron, ~$2.69 at RunPod (Secure Cloud), ~$3.99 at Lambda. Spot dips near $1.20/hr. Hyperscaler on-demand: ~$10–13/hr — the same card, 5–6× the money.
- H200 (141GB) — more memory, held or softened. About $2.30–6.31/hr on-demand: ~$2.30 at the FluidStack floor, ~$2.60 at GMI, ~$4.50 at Nebius (down from ~$5.50 in August), ~$6.31 at CoreWeave. Note a hyperscaler quirk: AWS's H200 via capacity blocks (~$4.98/GPU) is actually cheaper than its own H100 on-demand list rate, while Azure's H200 sits at the top of the range (~$10.60–13.78).
- B200 (Blackwell) — the month's real move. The on-demand floor cracked below $4: ~$3.70 at Spheron, ~$3.75 at Packet.ai (the cheapest in-stock rate GetDeploying tracked on Sept 3), ~$4.00 at GMI — down from August's ~$4.99 floor — with spot near $2.12–2.74 and the provider field widened to 30+. The mid-market still runs higher (~$5.50 Nebius, ~$8.60 CoreWeave), and hyperscaler B200 is ~$14–16/hr.
- GB200 / B300 (new this month) — the Grace-Blackwell superchips now rent by the hour, which they effectively didn't in August: GB200 from ~$8.00/hr at GMI, ~$10.50 at CoreWeave (NVL72), ~$16 at Oracle; B300 (Blackwell Ultra) runs roughly ~$7–18 depending on provider. GB300 is still quote-only.

...

## What changed since August#

If you read last month's map, here's the delta in four lines:

1. H100 floor: flat. ~$2 at GMI/Spheron, ~$1.49 at the Vast marketplace floor. But brand-name specialty on-demand firmed — Lambda's SXM rate climbed toward $3.99, so RunPod's ~$2.69 is now a more representative "cheap-but-reliable" number than August's headline $1.99.
2. H200: stable to softer. GMI still ~$2.60, Nebius eased to ~$4.50, CoreWeave ~$6.31. No dramatic move.
3. B200: floor down, availability up. The Blackwell on-demand floor fell from ~$4.99 to ~$3.70–4.00 and the provider count roughly doubled. This is where a founder's dollar moved the most.
4. The hyperscalers went UP. AWS raised H200 capacity-block prices ~15% on January 4, 2026 (Data Center Dynamics) — its first GPU price increase in roughly two decades. The premium for renting from a hyperscaler is widening, not narrowing.

...

- Discount specialty clouds (Vast.ai, GMI, RunPod, Spheron) optimize for cheap, no-commitment, by-the-hour access. Lowest sticker, fewest guarantees.
- Reserved/contract clouds (CoreWeave, and to a degree Nebius) are built for large, committed allocations. Their on-demand rate is deliberately high because on-demand isn't their product — reservations are.
- Hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle) bundle the GPU with a full platform, compliance surface, and enterprise support. You pay ~$12/hr for an H100 because you're buying everything around it — and, as January showed, they'll raise that rate when demand is tight.

...

How much does it cost to rent an H100 in September 2026?

On specialty GPU clouds, published on-demand H100 rates are still roughly $2–4 per GPU-hour: about $1.49 at the Vast.ai marketplace floor, ~$2.00 at GMI Cloud, ~$2.01 at Spheron, ~$2.69 at RunPod (Secure Cloud), and ~$3.99 at Lambda. The hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Oracle) sit far higher — roughly $10–13/hr for the identical card. Spot/preemptible H100 can dip near $1.20/hr where offered, with no availability guarantee. The floor is essentially flat versus August; a few brand-name specialty clouds (Lambda, Hyperbolic) actually nudged up.

...

They're published on-demand rates gathered in early September 2026 from public pricing pages and trackers, and they move constantly with supply, region, commitment, and stock. Use them for the shape of the market — the 5–7× spread, the sub-$4 B200 floor, the AWS increase — not as a live quote. Always confirm on the provider's own pricing page before you commit a dollar.

results.title: H100 Rental Prices Jump 22% in a Month as GPU Shortage Hits Firms and Labs - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: An Hye-ji, Intern Reporter
highlights: - Key summary: Vessl AI, a domestic neocloud company, raised the hourly rate for Nvidia H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39 on the 1st of this month, a 24.7% increase. The price adjustment marks the start of similar moves in Korea after U.S. neocloud firms including CoreWeave and Nebius successively raised GPU rental rates. Vessl AI procures most of its roughly 7,000 GPUs through leasing. According to Ornn, an AI computing trading platform, the hourly cloud rental rate for the H100 rose 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, reaching about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. The impact is spreading to industry and research, with some companies abandoning bids for government-led AI transformation projects because they could not secure GPUs, while universities and research institutes scale back the size of their research.

results.title: The same GPU, at very different prices · infratoapp
highlights:
The median gap between the cheapest and dearest seller of an identical card is 3.8×. The widest is the V100-16GB: $0.24 per GPU-hour at Verda (DataCrunch) against $2.85 at Runcrate, a gap of 11.8×. An H100 SXM 80GB — the card most of this market is actually built on — runs from $2.16 to $6.16 across 13 sellers, a gap of 2.8×.

These are headline on-demand rates, before any commitment discount, for the same part. Not a similar part, not a different memory configuration, and not one region against another.

results.title: Rental Rates for Older AI Chips Jump 25% as Demand Surges - Seoul Economic Daily
results.author: Seo Ji-hye, Kim Ji-young
highlights:
Vessl AI raised its hourly rate for Nvidia H100 graphics processing units by 24.7% starting this month, following a string of price increases by U.S. neocloud providers such as CoreWeave and Nebius amid a surge in demand for artificial intelligence computing. Supply has tightened not only for the newest chips but also for older models as demand for high-performance GPUs jumps. Other Korean cloud providers also expect to raise GPU rates depending on supply conditions, raising concerns that higher costs of securing GPUs will weigh on service development at Korean AI companies and on government AI transformation, or AX, projects.

Vessl AI on the 1st raised the hourly rate for H100 chips on its VESSL Cloud service to $2.98 from $2.39, according to AI industry sources on the 21st. The neocloud company counts leading Korean AI firms including Upstage and Motif Technologies among its clients and currently operates several thousand GPUs. It has secured about 7,000 GPUs, most of them leased rather than purchased outright. "It is hard to secure the volume we need for H100s — effectively, the price is whatever the seller names," a Vessl AI official said. "As AI demand grows, the number of customers wanting to use GPUs keeps rising, so a price adjustment was unavoidable." The company plans to expand its GPU fleet to about 10,000 units by the end of the year, but intends to keep adjusting rates flexibly to reflect supply conditions and procurement costs.

Other Korean AI cloud companies, including Elice, have also raised prices recently. In the past, rental rates for older AI GPUs fell when new models arrived, but prices for previous-generation chips are now rising as well. Hourly cloud rental rates for the H100 climbed 21.9% over the past month to $3.28 from $2.69, according to Ornn, an AI compute trading platform. That is about 70% of the price of the higher-end H200. Analysts say demand is spilling over to relatively older GPUs because supply of the newest chips cannot keep pace with surging computing demand.

highlights:
Flopper.io started as a specification database: peak TFLOPS by precision, memory, bandwidth and power for every datacenter GPU. Specs answer half of the buying question. ... The pipeline refreshes every six hours and has recorded every price change since 14 July 2026, so each GPU page now carries a price history alongside its spec sheet.

## What the Same GPU Costs, Cloud to Cloud

The spread is the story. On the day of publication, an on-demand H100 SXM5 80 GB (2022) is listed by 16 providers, and the most expensive listing costs nearly seven times the cheapest. The B200 (2024) shows the same pattern with a three-fold gap across eight clouds. Some of that gap is real: interconnect, storage, support and region all cost money. Some of it is simply price discovery that has not happened yet, because nobody was lining the numbers up.

On-demand, per-GPU, USD, as recorded on 9 September 2026. Spot, community and reserved listings are excluded from the range. Each GPU links to its live pricing page, which will have moved on by the time you read this.

...

- Per GPU, per hour, in USD. Node prices are divided by the GPU count. Monthly rates are divided by 730 hours. Non-USD prices are converted at the live exchange rate on the day of the sync.
- Pricing types are kept apart. On-demand (191 listings), spot or preemptible (31), marketplace community hosts (111) and reserved commitments (4) never share a row. The headline cheapest price on each GPU page is always on-demand, so an interruptible instance cannot masquerade as the market rate.
- Every listing maps to one canonical part. A provider's "H100" is matched to the exact variant it sells, SXM5 or PCIe, 80 GB or 94 GB, so a PCIe price never dilutes the SXM figure. Names the matcher cannot place are logged and dropped rather than guessed.
- Bad data is quarantined, not published. A listing that lands far outside its GPU's price band is held back and flagged for review. Median, dispersion and FP8-per-dollar figures on the pricing index are calculated so that a single bad listing cannot move them.

...

Public list prices only. Negotiated enterprise rates, reserved-capacity contracts and volume discounts are not published and are not tracked. Availability is shown where a provider publishes it, and a listed price does not guarantee capacity in the region you need. AWS and Google Cloud are the largest gaps in coverage; both publish pricing in formats that need heavier parsing and validation, and both are next on the list.

results.title: GPU Cloud Pricing in 2026: Are Prices Falling? | FastGPU
highlights:
Over 46 days to September 15, 2026, we tracked the cheapest on-demand price for every major GPU across 28 clouds, and the surprise was what did not happen: prices did not fall. In that study window the cheapest guaranteed H100 bounced between roughly $0.99 and $1.75 an hour with no sustained direction, and the newest Blackwell cards, rather than sliding as supply arrived, settled onto a flat plateau. What has not stalled is the gap between that floor and what the big clouds still charge for the identical chip. As of November 14, 2026, the same H100 rents from $1.73 an hour on the cheapest provider, while the cheapest hyperscaler on-demand rate is $5.38 ( Google Cloud) and Oracle lists it at $10.00 per GPU-hour, 5.8x the floor. When the study closed, Azure's own published on-demand rate worked out to about $12.29 per GPU-hour - Microsoft Azure Retail Prices API. The story of GPU pricing in 2026 is not a fall. It is a market that found its floor while the penalty for renting from the wrong place stays enormous.
